## Why "Jimcyclopedia"?

I've spent a long time as a student: a BS, two MS degrees, an MBA and a PhD.
Looking back, the handful of professors who did an amazing job all taught in a
way I was receptive to. I learn best from pictures, and from real-world examples
I can tie back to things I already know.

Most lessons I find offer good visuals or good examples, and often neither. With
help from large language models, I can now build the lessons I wish I'd had: an
encyclopedia of topics I find interesting, including machine learning, deep
learning, reinforcement learning, automotive engineering, finance, math and
controls. I use it to refresh my memory and to prepare for quantitative job
interviews.

If you've found this page, I hope you enjoy it and find it helpful.

## Neural networks to GenAI

A path from a single neuron to evaluating LLM agents. You don't have to take it
in order: each lesson lists only what it builds on, and the
[lesson map](map.qmd) shows the whole picture.
